annotations.keyFindings: Residents who chose monthly video debriefing gained 1.8 more points on a blinded 5 to 25 global rating scale over a year than residents who did not, after adjustment for training year.
annotations.limitations: Self-selected coaching; coached residents started with higher scores; 36 residents in two programmes.
annotations.notes: Closest design to the local question.

annotations.keyFindings: Blinded rating of edited cholecystectomy videos was reliable (intraclass correlation 0.79); two raters sufficed for change over time; about 12 minutes per edited video.
annotations.limitations: One procedure; raters from one country.
annotations.notes: Supplies the outcome measure and rater workload.

annotations.keyFindings: Peer and consultant video coaching improved blinded scores by similar amounts (3.6 and 3.9 points) over six months.
annotations.limitations: No uncoached group; cannot show that coaching itself works.
annotations.notes: Indirect: compares two forms of coaching.

annotations.keyFindings: 72 percent of residents would be filmed for coaching but only 38 percent for formal assessment; worries were greater among female and junior residents.
annotations.notes: Shapes consent and video retention rules.

annotations.keyFindings: Coached junior residents reached operating with passive help after a median of 14 operations against 19.
annotations.limitations: Unblinded raters; number of residents and year not reported.
annotations.notes: Supports autonomy as a secondary outcome only.

claims.text: Residents who chose monthly video debriefing with a coach gained 1.8 more points on a blinded global rating scale over one year than residents who did not.
claims.passage: a difference of 1.8 points (95 percent CI 0.4 to 3.2) after adjustment for training year
claims.interpretation: A plausible effect size for planning; confounded by self-selection.

claims.text: Two blinded raters scoring edited videos were enough to judge change in operative skill over time.
claims.passage: two raters were enough for decisions about change over time
claims.interpretation: The outcome can be measured with the consultants available if videos are edited.

claims.text: Most residents were willing to be filmed for coaching, but far fewer for formal assessment.
claims.passage: Most (72 percent) were willing to have operations filmed for coaching, but only 38 percent were willing for the same videos to be used in formal assessment.
claims.interpretation: Study videos must be kept out of assessment and deleted after rating.

synthesis: Five retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. One prospective comparison found that residents who chose video debriefing gained 1.8 more points on a blinded rating scale over a year, but self-selection may explain part of this. A randomised comparison showed peer and consultant coaching work similarly, without an uncoached group. Blinded rating of edited videos is reliable with two raters. Residents accept filming for coaching far more than for assessment. The evidence supports measuring coaching locally but gives only a rough effect size.
gradeRationale: One small non-randomised comparison, one randomised study without an uncoached group, and indirect or unblinded evidence; direction consistent, serious risk of bias and imprecision.
summary: Five retrieved records appraised; three claims recorded; overall certainty low.
